headline: High: Chatwoot’s broad egress plus next-ai-draw-io’s browser/MCP and API-key handling create default-path leakage and cascading-action risks; prompt-injection risk is lower but present via shared content flows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can ingest customer messages and integrations, while next-ai-draw-io uses browser and MCP-based tool use. If Chatwoot content is copied or routed into next-ai-draw-io, instruction-like text could steer tool use. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is pasted into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP inputs
IF a shared workspace or clipboard bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of raw support transcripts into agent prompts
Add a fixed prompt wrapper that strips instructions from imported text
Use separate workspaces for support content and diagram generation
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to imported content
requires-engineering: enforce allowlisted MCP tools only

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, and has broad network egress. next-ai-draw-io handles PDF/text/image files, uses external model APIs, and handles API keys. In default use, sensitive support content can flow into third-party inference or API calls, creating a realistic exfiltration path.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is included in files or prompts processed by next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io sends those inputs to external model APIs
mitigations: Restrict next-ai-draw-io to local-only models
Redact customer identifiers before export from Chatwoot
Block outbound network egress for the processing environment
Separate API keys from any workspace containing customer data
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before model calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and next-ai-draw-io can run multiple instances while Chatwoot exposes integrations. Even without explicit filesystem write claims, overlapping mutable external resources and concurrent API use can conflict, especially if both act on the same tickets or documents. Uncertainty about write surfaces pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured against the same external workspace or ticketing system
IF both agents write to the same downstream API-backed resource without locking
mitigations: Assign separate service accounts per agent
Limit each agent to disjoint resource namespaces
Turn off concurrent runs for shared resources
Add optimistic-lock checks on shared records
requires-engineering: introduce a coordinator for shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can surface customer messages and reports, and next-ai-draw-io performs AI-assisted visualization with natural-language commands. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative input, next-ai-draw-io may render or act on incorrect facts without verification. The downstream model/API calls make the blast radius broader than a simple formatting error.
conditions: IF Chatwoot-generated summaries or reports are fed directly into next-ai-draw-io
IF next-ai-draw-io executes actions or renders diagrams without a verification step
mitigations: Require human review before diagram generation
Use a validation step that checks source documents against summaries
Mark Chatwoot outputs as untrusted input in prompts
Limit next-ai-draw-io to read-only rendering mode
requires-engineering: add citation-preserving transformation checks

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while next-ai-draw-io handles files and sends content to multiple external AI providers. That creates a plausible retention/residency mismatch for regulated customer data, even though no specific jurisdiction or certification mismatch is documented. Because the pairwise compliance path is inferred, medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer data from Chatwoot is exported into next-ai-draw-io
IF any external model provider retains prompts or files beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of next-ai-draw-io inputs
Use providers with contractual retention controls
Document a data-flow map for support content
Pseudonymize customer records before processing
requires-engineering: enforce residency-aware routing
